children: Meetings with SMBC, SEB, HPS Investment Partners, B Capital Group and MUFG focused on expanding financing and investment opportunities in India

Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman held meetings with senior executives of five global financial institutions and investment firms in Singapore to discuss investment and financing opportunities in India across infrastructure, private credit, artificial intelligence (AI), renewable energy and housing finance.

According to posts shared by the Ministry of Finance on X, the meetings involved representatives from Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation (SMBC), Skandinaviska Enskilda Banken (SEB), HPS Investment Partners, B Capital Group and Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group (MUFG).
During her meeting with HPS Investment Partners Chief Executive Officer Scott Kapnick, Sitharaman discussed private credit, structured finance and long-term financing for businesses.

According to the ministry, she encouraged HPS to explore setting up a fund in Gujarat International Finance Tec-City's International Financial Services Centre (GIFT IFSC) and collaborating with the National Investment and Infrastructure Fund (NIIF) to mobilise financing for large infrastructure projects in India.
HPS highlighted the potential for debt capital to complement equity investments, the ministry said.

Sitharaman's meeting with MUFG Chief Executive for Asia Pacific Yukinobu Saeki focused on expanding the bank's engagement in India across capital markets, infrastructure and project finance, renewable energy and mergers and acquisitions financing.
She also encouraged greater engagement with the National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development (NaBFID) to support infrastructure financing.
The discussions covered financing for Indian small and medium enterprises and regulatory roadshows aimed at enhancing market transparency and governance.
SEB Explores Investment Opportunities
During her meeting with SEB Chairperson Marcus Wallenberg, Sitharaman discussed India's economic outlook and ways to strengthen investment flows from European institutional investors.
According to the ministry, SEB highlighted opportunities in energy, data centres, information technology and tax services, healthcare, financial services and housing finance.
The discussions also covered sustainable finance, private equity investments in non-banking financial companies (NBFCs), the green transition and skill development.
Sitharaman met SMBC Managing Executive Officer and Co-Head for Asia Pacific Rajeev Kannan to discuss expanding the bank's activities in India.
The discussions included affordable housing finance, financing for NBFCs, trade finance and other priority sectors.
Sitharaman encouraged SMBC to explore investment and financing opportunities through NIIF and GIFT IFSC, particularly in aircraft leasing, according to the ministry.
B Capital Discusses AI Opportunities
Separately, Sitharaman met B Capital Group Co-founder and Chief Executive Officer Raj Ganguly to discuss sovereign AI and the broader AI ecosystem.
She highlighted India's potential in AI services and encouraged the firm to explore applications of the technology in banking and financial services.
The ministry said B Capital emphasised the importance of a stable currency and predictable, transparent tax policies for investors.

The meetings focused on potential avenues to increase financing for Indian businesses and infrastructure and attract investment across technology, energy and other sectors. The ministry's posts did not specify any investment commitments or agreements arising from the discussions.
